Score: the share of the 3,288 Logic and Math questions together (setups that finished both) answered right, the whisker its 95% interval. # is the tier: rows in one tier are not told apart by the paired test (a line separates tiers); – : with web or sample, not tiered.

Class: by the maker's total parameters, or by list price when the size is undisclosed *

Size by total parameters, as disclosed by the maker (for MoE models the label also shows active parameters): Tiny under 6B · Small 6B–15B · Medium over 15B up to 40B · Large over 40B. Models of undisclosed size, by standard list price per 1M input tokens: Efficient up to $0.50 · Workhorse up to $3 · Flagship over $3. Undisclosed: neither a disclosed size nor a list price.

One row per model: its highest reasoning setting (off < low < medium < high), a model with one setup that setup; a tie by the earliest run, then the name. Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2: its API setup on every part (its other setup is under other settings). The model's other settings are under its row; All setups lists every setup.

# is the tier: rows in accuracy order, the top row starts Tier 1, a row joins the tier unless the paired test behind the tie letters (exact McNemar, Holm-corrected over all pairs of tiered rows in view, p < 0.05) separates it from the tier's top row; otherwise it starts the next tier. – : with web or sample, not tiered.

Chat and decision models on Logic

Each bar is a leaderboard row on Logic with its 95% interval: the chat models and the highest decision models. A chat model writes a reply that ends in a letter; a decision model scores the five options and picks one.

Every setup on Logic →

Logic and Math, setup by setup

One dot per setup that has finished both benchmarks (60 setups, chat models included): across, its Logic accuracy; up, its Math accuracy; the whiskers are 95% intervals. The count is of setups, not models (Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2's two setups count twice). Above the dashed line a setup does better on Math.

Logic and Math pooled, every setup →

Numerical reasoning is the decision models' lowest-scoring logic topic: median 33.3%, against verbal reasoning 50.0%, formal logic 76.5%

The median accuracy of the finished setups on each logic topic, decision models and chat models apart; it is the lowest topic for 43 of the 44 decision setups. Medians over finished runs only.

Every setup by topic →

How the scores work

  • One question per request. A decision model scores the five options and picks one; a chat model writes a reply that ends in a letter.
  • Accuracy is right / all questions. No partial credit; a reply without a letter counts as wrong.
  • Uncertainty is shown. Intervals are 95% Wilson intervals; two setups are tied unless a paired exact test (McNemar) separates them after Holm's correction.
  • Costs are what a run would cost. The provider's price × the usage its API reported (unmarked), the maker's list price × our token counts (“list”), or for our own hardware its wall-clock time from first to last answer while it was running (pauses, estimated from gaps of more than 10 minutes between answers, left out), × $2.49/h per RTX PRO 6000 or × $0.213/h per DGX Spark, shown as “On our NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB)” or “On our NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10)” (at most: runs that shared the hardware are each charged in full).
  • The questions are English translations from six published Turkish question books; about a third of the logic questions and nearly all math questions are past public questions of ÖSYM, Turkey's national exam centre.
